20	|---|---|
21	| `person` | `people/<slug>.md` |
22	| `area` | `areas/<slug>.md` |
23	| `topic` | `topics/<slug>.md` |

25	| `chunk` | `sources/<source-slug>/<slug>.md`; the slug is `<source-slug>-ch-<nn>` |
26

28

30

When the answer needs a second subject ("who employs the supervisor of X"), follow the link: find its row in `index.md`, then open it by path. A link to a slug with no index row means the brain has nothing on it.

# Gateway skill: navigating the brain

You answer questions from a brain: a folder of markdown nodes with an `index.md` at its root. You are told the brain's root path. Everything you say must come from nodes you opened. Follow these steps in order.

## 1. Read `index.md` first, and only it

Open `<brain>/index.md` before any other file. It has one row per node: `slug`, `type`, `aliases`, `id`, `description`. Do not list, glob or search the brain's folders: the index is the map.

## 2. Pick candidates from the index

Choose the rows whose description or aliases fit the question. Match names loosely: lowercase, ignore accents, treat spaces, underscores and hyphens alike (`Inés Navarro`, `ines navarro` and `ines-navarro` are the same name).

If no row plausibly fits, stop and go to step 6. Do not open a node just to see what is in it.

## 3. Open nodes by path

The path follows from the row:

| type | path |
|---|---|
| `person` | `people/<slug>.md` |
| `area` | `areas/<slug>.md` |
| `topic` | `topics/<slug>.md` |
| `source` | `sources/<slug>.md` |
| `chunk` | `sources/<source-slug>/<slug>.md`; the slug is `<source-slug>-ch-<nn>` |

Open the best candidate first. Open more only when the question needs it. Aim for five files or fewer, `index.md` included.

## 4. Follow links for multi-step questions

A node's `## Links` lines name related nodes as `[[slug]]`, with the relation in words. When the answer needs a second subject ("who employs the supervisor of X"), follow the link: find its row in `index.md`, then open it by path. A link to a slug with no index row means the brain has nothing on it.

## 5. Page questions go through the chunk

For a question about a section, chapter or page of a source, open the chunk, not just the source. The chunk's `pages` field gives its page range, and its facts cite pages as `(src: <source> p.<n>, <date>)`. Quote both in the answer.

Within an opened file you may search for the exact passage. Never search across files.

## 6. Answer only from what you opened

Each fact line reads `- [tag] <fact> (src: <source>, <date>)`. The **last** bracketed group is always the source.

- Answer from fact lines only. Never add knowledge of your own, and never infer beyond what a fact says.
- `[stated]` and `[observed]` facts you may give as facts. A `[derived]` fact is an agent's inference: say so ("an agent concluded that…").
- A changed fact reads `<new> (was <old>, changed <date>[ by <change source>])`. When asked about history, give the current value, the old value, the change date and, if named, what changed it. The final bracketed group is still the original source, such as a page; cite it for the fact.
- If the opened nodes do not contain the answer, say **"I don't have that"**, and say what you checked. Do not stretch a related fact into an answer. Do not answer partly from general knowledge. A confident wrong answer is the worst outcome.

## 7. Report what you opened

End every answer with the files you opened, in order, as paths relative to the brain root.

1	---
2	id: b37e4091-5137-4ad1-8044-2a9fb9ac5dba
3	slug: apollo-11-mission-report-ch-05
4	name: "Apollo 11 Mission Report, Section 5.3: Powered Descent"
5	type: chunk
6	description: "Section 5.3, pages 5-4 to 5-6: five computer alarms, crater avoidance, manual control, landing point and propellant use"
7	created: 2026-10-24
8	updated: 2026-10-24
9	aliases: []
10	pages: "5-4 to 5-6"
11	---
12	
13	## Facts
14	
15	- [stated] Throttle reduction came at 386 seconds after ignition against 384 predicted, indicating nominal engine performance (src: Apollo 11 Mission Report p.5-4, 2026-10-24)
16	- [stated] The first of five computer alarms came about 5 minutes after descent initiation (src: Apollo 11 Mission Report p.5-4, 2026-10-24)
17	- [stated] High gate and the switch to program P64 came at 7129 feet at 125 feet per second (src: Apollo 11 Mission Report p.5-4, 2026-10-24)
18	- [stated] The approach path led into a large crater, forcing an unplanned redesignation (src: Apollo 11 Mission Report p.5-4, 2026-10-24)
19	- [stated] Manual control began at about 600 feet and the craft landed about 1100 feet downrange of the initial aim point (src: Apollo 11 Mission Report p.5-5, 2026-10-24)
20	- [stated] About 95 pounds of reaction control propellant were used against 40 predicted (src: Apollo 11 Mission Report p.5-6, 2026-10-24)
21	- [stated] Manual-mode reaction control use was 51 pounds, about 1.5 times the automatic rate (src: Apollo 11 Mission Report p.5-6, 2026-10-24)

## Facts

- [stated] Throttle reduction came at 386 seconds after ignition against 384 predicted, indicating nominal engine performance (src: Apollo 11 Mission Report p.5-4, 2026-10-24)
- [stated] The first of five computer alarms came about 5 minutes after descent initiation (src: Apollo 11 Mission Report p.5-4, 2026-10-24)
- [stated] High gate and the switch to program P64 came at 7129 feet at 125 feet per second (src: Apollo 11 Mission Report p.5-4, 2026-10-24)
- [stated] The approach path led into a large crater, forcing an unplanned redesignation (src: Apollo 11 Mission Report p.5-4, 2026-10-24)
- [stated] Manual control began at about 600 feet and the craft landed about 1100 feet downrange of the initial aim point (src: Apollo 11 Mission Report p.5-5, 2026-10-24)
- [stated] About 95 pounds of reaction control propellant were used against 40 predicted (src: Apollo 11 Mission Report p.5-6, 2026-10-24)
- [stated] Manual-mode reaction control use was 51 pounds, about 1.5 times the automatic rate (src: Apollo 11 Mission Report p.5-6, 2026-10-24)
